name: Paris
tagline: Art, Cuisine, and Romance in the World's Most Celebrated City
description: Paris needs no introduction — the City of Light offers unrivaled art, architecture, gastronomy, and cultural depth. While expensive by European standards, Paris rewards those who can afford it with a quality of life few cities can match. World-class healthcare, exceptional public transit, and a lifestyle built around beauty, conversation, and long meals make it a dream for culturally-minded retirees willing to pay the premium.

quickFacts.visa: 90-day Schengen visa-free for US citizens. Visitor visa (Type D) for long stays — requires proof of sufficient funds and no employment. Path to residency after 5 years of continuous stay.
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate — safe overall but petty crime and pickpocketing common in tourist areas
quickFacts.nearestAirport: Charles de Gaulle Airport (CDG) — 45 min from city center; Orly Airport (ORY) — 30 min
quickFacts.climate: Oceanic-continental with mild summers (20-25°C) and cool winters (3-7°C). Frequent overcast skies and light rain year-round.

housing.description: Furnished studio in the 19th or 20th, or a near suburb like Montreuil, Bagnolet, or Pantin

dining.description: Modest bistro/cheap eats; mostly home cooking

1M.lifestyle: A furnished studio in the 19th or 20th, or a near suburb like Montreuil or Pantin, with a Navigo pass covering the whole metro/RER/bus network. Boulangerie breakfasts and prix-fixe lunch menus anchor the food budget, with most dinners cooked at home. Health cover is an entry private/international plan pitched at the long-stay visa requirement. The apartment is small and restaurant dinners are occasional, but free-museum Sundays, Seine-side walks, and the Luxembourg Gardens make the cultural access remarkable for the money.

2M.lifestyle: A one-bedroom in the 11th, 12th, 15th, or 18th, eating out more freely and shopping the markets for better produce. Health cover adds a fuller private layer, and there is room for a mid-tier gym, more culture, and nightlife. Comfortable, centrally-placed Paris living below the prestige-arrondissement premium.

housing.description: Comfortable 1-bedroom in a desirable central arrondissement — the Marais (3rd/4th), the 9th, 11th, or 5th

transportation.description: Navigo pass plus Vélib and regular taxis

entertainment.description: Full gym, theatre, museums, dining-out culture

3M.lifestyle: A comfortable one-bedroom in a desirable central arrondissement — the Marais, the 9th, 11th, or 5th. Dining out is a regular pleasure, health cover is a comprehensive international plan, and the Navigo pass plus Vélib and regular taxis cover the city. Full gym, theatre, museums, and the long-lunch culture are all within reach, with genuine margin each month — affluent Parisian life without a car.

housing.description: Spacious high-standard 1-bedroom in a prestige arrondissement (6th, 7th, 8th, or 16th)

transportation.description: Navigo pass plus frequent taxis and an occasional car service (first tier a car appears)

5M.lifestyle: A spacious, high-standard one-bedroom in a prestige arrondissement (6th, 7th, 8th, or 16th), with a weekly housekeeper. Dining is frequent and fine, a premium international health plan removes friction, and a car service joins the Navigo pass and taxis. A premium club, opera and culture, and short-haul travel fill out an upper-affluent life in the heart of the city.

housing.description: Grand Haussmannian apartment in the Golden Triangle near Avenue Montaigne, or a prestige 7th/8th/16th address

healthcare.description: Top-tier international concierge, worldwide incl. US

entertainment.description: Private clubs, opera boxes, premium culture

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeper several times a week (~50 hrs/mo @ ~€21/hr)

10M.lifestyle: A grand Haussmannian apartment in the Golden Triangle near Avenue Montaigne, kept by a housekeeper several times a week. Dining ranges across the city's Michelin tables, health cover is top-tier international concierge, and a car with a chauffeur handles evenings. The discretionary budget funds private clubs, opera boxes, a wine cellar, and constant travel. Paris absorbs large budgets, but this is the genuine top of the market — a prime address, staff on hand, and the city's culture wide open.
